post.summary: Super Admin login
post.description: Validates email and password credentials. When MFA is enabled on the account a one-time code is sent via email and the response contains a short-lived ``temp_token`` instead of a full access token. Submit that ``temp_token`` together with the received code to ``POST /auth/mfa/verify`` to obtain a full JWT. After repeated failures the account is progressively locked following a J-curve schedule; the lock duration doubles with every additional failed attempt beyond the stage-2 threshold.

post.summary: Request a password reset link
post.description: Sends a one-time password reset link to the registered email address. The response is always identical regardless of whether the email is registered, to prevent user enumeration.

post.summary: Verify invite token
post.description: Verify if an invite token is valid without consuming it.

post.summary: Verify reset password token
post.description: Verify if a reset password token is valid without consuming it.

post.summary: Reset password using a one-time token
post.description: Validates the one-time token from the reset or invitation email and sets a new password.  Invited accounts (``invitation_status='Pending'``) are automatically transitioned to ``'Accepted'`` on success.  Tokens expire after 24 hours and are single-use.

post.summary: Resend MFA one-time code
post.description: Generates a new MFA code if the previous 2-minute window has expired.

post.summary: Verify MFA one-time code
post.description: Validates the emailed OTP against the ``temp_token`` issued during the ``/login`` step. Returns a full JWT access token on success. The temp token expires after 2 minutes. Repeated failures trigger progressive MFA lockouts on the same J-curve schedule as login failures.

post.summary: Log out the current session
post.description: Revokes the bearer access token by persisting its ``jti`` claim in the ``revoked_tokens`` table.  Subsequent requests using the same token are rejected with HTTP 401 even if the token has not yet expired. The client should discard the token after calling this endpoint.

post.summary: Update current user's password
post.description: Updates the password for the currently authenticated user.

get.description: Returns a lightweight list of active organizations with just org_id and name.

post.summary: Platform summary metrics and upload graph
post.description: Returns global platform metrics and organization-specific upload activity graph if org_id is provided in the request payload.

post.summary: List all organizations
post.description: Returns a paginated, filtered list of organizations ordered by creation date (newest first). Use ``search`` for a cross-field keyword search, ``status`` / ``invitation_status`` for exact-match select filters, and date range parameters to filter by registration date.

post.summary: List all deleted organizations
post.description: Returns a paginated list of soft-deleted organizations ordered by deletion date (newest first). Use ``search`` for a cross-field keyword search and ``status`` / ``invitation_status`` for exact-match select filters. Useful for recovery or audit purposes before hard delete.

post.summary: Create organization and trigger tenant DB provisioning
post.description: Creates an Organization record in the master DB with status ``'Provisioning'`` and immediately returns. A background task then: (1) creates a dedicated PostgreSQL database, (2) runs Alembic migrations, (3) seeds the initial Org Admin, (4) encrypts and stores the tenant DB URL, and (5) updates status to ``'Active'`` or ``'Failed'``.

put.description: Activate or deactivate an organization by its human-readable ``org_id``.

delete.description: Soft deletes an organization, hiding it from normal queries. Hard delete occurs after the retention period.

post.summary: Restore a deleted organization
post.description: Restores a soft-deleted organization, making it visible in normal queries again.

delete.description: Hard deletes a soft-deleted organization immediately (irreversible). Use this to free up an email address before the retention period expires.

post.summary: Get organization detail
post.description: Returns a single organization by its human-readable ``org_id``.

get.description: Returns the available organization statuses (Active/Inactive) for dropdown menus.
Returns total users, active users, and pending invitations for Super Admins.

post.summary: List Super Admin users (Search)
post.description: Returns a paginated, filtered list of Super Admin accounts ordered by creation date (newest first). Use ``search`` for a cross-field keyword search, ``role`` / ``status`` for select filters, and the ``*_from`` / ``*_to`` parameters for date-range filters in the request body.

post.summary: Invite a Super Admin user
post.description: Creates a Super Admin account with ``invitation_status='Pending'``. The user should later accept the invitation to update their status.

delete.summary: Soft delete a Super Admin user
delete.description: Soft deletes a Super Admin, hiding them from normal queries. Hard delete occurs after the retention period.

patch.description: Partially update ``first_name``, ``last_name``, ``contact_number``, ``mfa_enabled``, ``Role`` and/or ``Status``. Only supplied fields are changed. ``contact_number`` is stored KMS-encrypted. Hierarchy rules apply.

post.summary: Recover a deleted Super Admin user
post.description: Restores a soft-deleted Super Admin within the retention window, making the email address available again and restoring the account to Active status.

delete.summary: Permanently delete a Super Admin user
delete.description: Hard deletes a soft-deleted Super Admin account immediately (irreversible). Use this to free up an email address before the retention period expires.

put.summary: Assign a role to a user
put.description: Change the role of a Super Admin account. ``super_user`` can assign any role. ``admin`` can only assign ``reviewer`` or ``viewer`` and only to users who are not ``super_user`` or ``admin``.

post.summary: Unlock a permanently locked Super Admin account
post.description: Resets all login and MFA failure counters to zero, clears any time-based lockout window, and restores the account status to ``Active``.  Use this after a permanently locked account has been reviewed and approved for re-access. A 404 is returned if the user does not exist; a 400 is returned if the account is not currently in a locked state.

post.summary: Get Super Admin user detail
post.description: Returns a single Super Admin account by UUID passed in the request body.

put.summary: Activate or deactivate a Super Admin account
put.description: Sets the account ``status`` to ``'Active'`` or ``'Inactive'``. Hierarchy rules apply: you may only update users with a lower authority level than your own.

patch.summary: Update the currently logged-in user's profile
patch.description: Allows the authenticated user to update their own profile details: name, contact number, MFA, and profile picture key.

post.summary: Resend invitation email to a pending Super Admin
post.description: Generates a fresh one-time invitation token and sends a new invitation email.  Only works when ``invitation_status`` is ``'Pending'``.

put.summary: Store the blob name for a user profile picture
put.description: The frontend uploads the image directly to Azure Storage and then calls this endpoint with the resulting blob name.  We store the name and return a short-lived presigned GET URL for immediate display.

post.summary: List all audit log entries
post.description: Returns paginated, filtered platform-level audit events ordered most-recent first. Audit logs are immutable and cannot be deleted via the API. Use ``GET /audit-logs/verify`` to detect any tampering.

get.summary: Fetch distinct audit log filter options
get.description: Returns the distinct ``modules`` and ``actions`` present in the audit log so frontends can populate filter dropdowns dynamically.

post.summary: Export filtered audit logs as CSV or Excel
post.description: Returns an exported file of audit log entries matching the supplied filters. Accepts the same filter parameters as ``POST /audit-logs/list`` but ignores ``page``/``limit`` — the full result set is returned (hard cap: 10,000 rows).

get.description: Walks the entire audit log chain and verifies SHA-256 hash linkage. Reports the sequence number and reason of the first detected violation if the chain has been tampered with.
Returns the active progressive lockout configuration for login and MFA failures.  Defaults are seeded automatically on first access and can be adjusted without redeploying the application.

put.description: Partially update the progressive lockout thresholds and durations.  Only supplied fields are updated; omitted fields retain their current values.  Changes take effect immediately on the next authentication request — no restart required.  The stage-1 threshold must be less than the stage-2 threshold.

post.summary: Verify Tenant MFA code

Initiate forgot-password flow
post.description:
Initiate the forgot-password flow by emailing a one-time reset link.

The endpoint always returns a generic success message — even when the
supplied email is not registered — to prevent user enumeration.

Audit actions emitted:

* ``PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED`` — A valid account was found and a token issued.

Args:
    payload: Request body containing the user's ``email``.
    request: Injected FastAPI request object; used to extract the client IP.
    master_session: Injected async database session (master DB).

Returns:
    A generic success dict regardless of whether the email was found.

post.summary: Verify reset password token
post.description: Verify if a reset password token is valid without consuming it.

post.summary: Reset password using a token
post.description:
Set a new password using a valid one-time token.

Handles both the forgot-password flow and first-time password setting
for newly invited Tenant Users.  On success:

* The user's ``hashed_password`` is updated.
* If ``invitation_status == 'Pending'`` it is set to ``'Accepted'``.
* The token fields are cleared so the token cannot be reused.

Audit actions emitted:

* ``PASSWORD_RESET_COMPLETED`` — Password updated via a reset token.
* ``INVITE_ACCEPTED``          — Invited user set their first password.

Args:
    payload: Request body containing the ``token``, ``new_password``,
        ``confirm_password``, and ``org_id``.
    master_session: Injected async database session (master DB).

Returns:
    A success dict with a confirmation message.

Raises:
    HTTPException 400: Token is invalid, expired, or already consumed.

post.summary: Log out the current session
post.description:
Revoke the current access token and write an audit log entry.

Audit events emitted:

* ``LOGOUT`` — Token successfully blacklisted.

Args:
    request: Injected FastAPI request object; used to extract the
        client IP for the audit log.
    current_user: Injected user context from the bearer token.
    master_session: Injected async database session (master DB).

Returns:
    A success message dict.

post.summary: Submit a claim for AI validation
post.description:
1. Connects to the tenant database based on the active user session.
2. Verifies that the patient and provider exist.
3. Calls the LLM server to initiate validation and retrieve the job_id.
4. Creates the Claim record in the tenant DB using id=job_id.
5. Creates Document records for each uploaded file url referencing the job_id.
6. Returns the job_id as claim_id, and the claim number.

SecurityPolicyUpdateRequest.title: SecurityPolicyUpdateRequest
SecurityPolicyUpdateRequest.description:
Request body for ``PUT /superadmin/security-policy``.

All fields are optional; omitted fields retain their current values.
The J-curve lockout schedule is governed by six independent thresholds
(three for login, three for MFA).

Stage constraints enforced by the service layer:
``stage1_threshold`` must be < ``stage2_threshold``.
Block minutes must be positive.  Multiplier must be ≥ 1.0.
